display.title: Episode 18: The Stolen Purse (Erev Pesach)
display.summary_short: On the eve of Pesach the Rebbe of Chortkov's tzedakah money vanishes, and his loyal servant confesses to a theft he never committed. Plus an amen for the Rebbe's 80th birthday and Pesach reminders.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the eve of Erev Pesach 5742. Uncle Yossi thanks listeners, speaks of uniting children through Torah and mitzvos to bring Moshiach, and teaches a five-word Pesach song from Nishmas, 'You freed us from Egypt and redeemed us from slavery', before a joyful march. The story: the Rebbe of Chortkov kept a fund for the poor, and only his honest servant, Meir Anshel, had the key. Just before Pesach the purse of 500 gold coins disappears. A yeshivah student leads the Shema. Meir Anshel, seeing the Rebbe's sorrow for the poor, 'confesses' and brings back the money, until a Polish count returns the real purse, dropped by a maid who had stolen it. The Rebbe blesses Meir Anshel for his kindness, and Uncle Yossi reveals that his family name was Rothschild. Next, Uncle Yossi explains that children's prayers and amens are especially precious, and all the children answer amen to a blessing for the Rebbe's 80th birthday on Yud-Aleph Nissan. The show ends with reminders to sell chametz and eat matzah at both Sedorim, thanks to supporters, and the time of next week's program.
display.lesson: A kind and generous heart is blessed by Hashem; and the pure prayers and amens of children reach Hashem first.
